paths.description: Homepage/editorial landing: global navigation, hero content, ads, preferences, mobile layout, performance, network, discoverability, and memory.
Latest-articles listing: representative editorial index/card template.
Community/forum listing: high-interaction content archetype and advertising density.
Primary account registration form: labels, autofill, focus, task completion, and account safety.
Unknown-route recovery: representative HTTP/application failure state.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot remains the same white surface as the default screenshot; computed html/body color-scheme is normal and CSS inspection found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control, and ad-container colors.

findings.summary: High-contrast resilience is weak.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 107 color-contrast failures, and the stylesheet has no prefers-contrast treatment while many controls use pale grey text.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG contrast minimums and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations without suppressing system colors.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use meaningful View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Representative routes are conventional full navigations; DOM/CSS inspection found no authored transition rules beyond third-party reset declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document view transitions for navigation between article, listing, forum, and account templates, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-position-aware navigation cue.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 14,852 px tall at mobile width, yet screenshots and inspected CSS show static chrome with no progress indicator or authored scroll-state behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a lightweight sticky header or progress cue that responds to scroll state without covering content.

findings.summary: Advertising repeatedly obscures primary content and controls.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show fixed bottom ads covering article cards, forum content, signup fields, and the 404 recovery surface; desktop also shows a large floating ad over the hero.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove load-time overlays from primary content, reserve non-overlapping ad slots, and require explicit interaction for overlays.

findings.summary: Injected promotional overlays use custom high-z-index div/iframe chrome.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no dialog, popover, or details primitives while injected Yektanet styles create fixed overlays up to z-index 99,999,999 with custom close controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic dialog/popover primitives for site-owned overlays and constrain third-party ad containers to non-modal, clearly dismissible slots.

findings.summary: Commercial chrome competes with the editorial experience.
findings.evidence: Every representative mobile screenshot gives substantial first-viewport area to banner and floating advertising, including overlapping stacked promotions on discussion and signup.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an ad density budget, eliminate overlapping formats, and prioritize one clear content column and task area.

findings.summary: The mobile layout has measurable horizontal overflow.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout probe reported scrollWidth 366 against a 360 px visual viewport, for 6 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the overflowing width/margin and use intrinsic sizing with max-inline-size:100%.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport styling rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across home, article, forum, and signup templates found no authored @container rules; many ad and card rules use fixed pixel widths and global media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable card/navigation regions and size-aware @container rules for their internal layout.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and several targets are too small.
findings.evidence: A focused signup navigation link computed to outline:none and box-shadow:none; Lighthouse also reported 9 insufficiently sized or spaced targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible style and raise interactive targets to at least 24x24 CSS px with adequate spacing, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The signup journey is obstructed by advertising.
findings.evidence: The signup mobile screenshot shows a large floating video promotion covering password/captcha fields in the primary registration form.
findings.suggestedFix: Exclude account and form journeys from floating ad formats and keep all required fields and the submit action continuously visible.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance misses the LCP quality bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.5 s, LCP 10.6 s, Speed Index 6.3 s, and Time to Interactive 11.9 s (performance 0.59); a separate trace measured LCP 2.67 s, showing material run variance.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image/content, reduce third-party contention, and validate on representative mobile network/CPU conditions.

findings.summary: Images and noncritical resources are delivered inefficiently.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 89 below-fold images without lazy loading, 73 without srcset, 91 legacy-format images, and 16 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, provide responsive srcset/sizes, use modern formats, and explicitly prioritize only the LCP image.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 174 KiB unused JavaScript and 38 KiB unused CSS; the main CSS bundle was 93% unused in the sampled load.
findings.suggestedFix: Split template-specific bundles and conditionally load advertising/analytics code only where it provides value.

findings.summary: Several interactive controls lack accessible names or valid ARIA structure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 7 unnamed buttons, 4 unnamed links, one required-children ARIA failure, and two presentation-role conflicts.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native controls and give every interactive element a visible or programmatic name with valid roles and relationships.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail contrast requirements at scale.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 107 elements with insufficient foreground/background contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the color tokens and ad/control states to meet WCAG AA contrast in every template and state.

findings.summary: Document structure and keyboard focus are not robust.
findings.evidence: All four inspected templates had zero h1 and zero main elements; Lighthouse found seven heading-order failures and no main landmark, while the focus probe showed no visible focus ring.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1 and a main landmark per template, repair heading order, and implement persistent :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Small targets and slight overflow undermine reflow usability.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 9 target-size failures and the 360 px layout had 6 px horizontal overflow; the viewport meta itself permits scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target dimensions/spacing and remove overflow, then verify at 200% zoom and narrow reflow widths.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a failed network request.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit failed because a resource returned HTTP 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or remove the broken resource reference and keep console/network error monitoring in release checks.

findings.summary: Asset markup and responsive image delivery need cleanup.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 3 images without dimensions, 16 oversized images, and 73 without responsive sources; Lighthouse also reported a low-resolution mobile logo.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide intrinsic dimensions, correct aspect ratios, and appropriately sized responsive sources for every image.

findings.summary: robots.txt contains an invalid directive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO reported “Allow /sitemap” on line 4 as syntax not understood; links and viewport otherwise passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct robots.txt syntax and reference the sitemap with a valid Sitemap: directive.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP is missing; all 6 observed first-party cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP and set Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite value on all cookies.

findings.summary: The page has a broad tracking and advertising footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 19 third-party origins and known Clarity, Google Tag Manager, and DoubleClick endpoints; Lighthouse found third-party cookies and the screenshots show multiple ad formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit necessity, consent, retention, and payloads for each vendor; remove redundant trackers and defer nonessential collection until informed consent.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks modern phishing-resistant options.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse confirmed no permission prompts on load, but signup/sign-in DOM exposes password fields and no WebAuthn/passkey affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside recovery-safe fallback methods.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strict Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and enforce CSP with frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: Third-party overlays create fragile, obstructed runtime states.
findings.evidence: Fixed Yektanet containers use extreme z-index values and overlap form and error-recovery content at mobile sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Isolate ad scripts, cap their stacking context, reserve layout space, and ensure close/recovery controls remain reachable.

findings.summary: Persian pages do not declare document direction.
findings.evidence: All inspected templates set lang="fa" but neither html nor body declares dir="rtl"; CSS includes many physical left/right declarations despite some logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir="rtl" at the document root and migrate reusable layout rules to logical properties.

findings.summary: Advertisements are visually intrusive and insufficiently separated from key tasks.
findings.evidence: Floating promotions cover editorial, forum, registration, and 404 surfaces; some include only tiny branding/close affordances and resemble in-page content.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label ads, prohibit overlap with primary UI, make dismissal obvious, and avoid disruptive formats on sensitive account paths.

findings.summary: Form errors are not exposed with modern accessible state semantics.
findings.evidence: Signup markup contains required validation messages but no aria-live or aria-invalid, and several fields lack associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, set aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and announce a concise error summary in a live region.

findings.summary: Registration input assistance is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The telephone field has autocomplete="off" and no associated label; confirm-password and captcha fields also lack associated labels, while password has new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use stable names and correct autocomplete tokens (tel, username, new-password) with explicit labels for every field.

findings.summary: The account flow is neither distraction-free nor proportionate.
findings.evidence: A floating advertisement covers registration fields, and the authentication surface offers passwords without a passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove floating ads from account flows, keep commitments clear, and add phishing-resistant authentication and safe recovery.

findings.summary: The image strategy wastes bandwidth and decoding work.
findings.evidence: Of 93 images, 91 are legacy formats, 73 lack srcset, 89 below-fold images are not lazy, and 16 are oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, use srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and size assets to rendered dimensions.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics work is disproportionate.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe recorded 19 third-party origins; Lighthouse attributes the largest unused-JS savings to GTM/gtag and measured 174 KiB unused JavaScript overall.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics, batch events, and load ad/analytics work conditionally and at lower priority.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes a large share of the page budget.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse transferred 1,535 KiB and two Google tag scripts were among the four largest resources; tracker evidence found 19 third-party origins and multiple simultaneous ad formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, consolidate vendors, and defer media/ads until below the primary content.

taskList.title: Remove overlapping ad formats from content, account, and recovery paths
Fix accessible names, landmarks, headings, contrast, focus, and target sizes
Harden CSP, cookie attributes, privacy policies, and tracker minimisation
Improve mobile LCP and responsive image delivery
Repair signup labels, validation announcements, autocomplete, and passkey support
Adopt intrinsic/container-level responsive layout and RTL logical properties
Correct robots.txt and eliminate console/asset errors
